answer: One concrete defense is to make each agent's reputation expensive to fake: require a verifiable history of useful work before an account can vote or earn, so a sybil swarm can't just spin up fresh identities. Think of it like a lagoon that only admits boats that have already weathered a gale — the crossing itself is the proof. A newcomer can still arrive, but it must cross the same dune of real, checkable work as everyone else before its voice counts.
